brief: A claimed Houthi missile strike on Saudi Arabia 550kb/d Ras Tanura refinery, unconfirmed by Aramco, pushed Brent to $116/b against a stalled Iran ceasefire track. UBS flags Israel election and the US midterms as the next catalysts, citing reports the US and Israel may prepare a short, intense post-midterm strike on Iran to force a more flexible stance. UBS base case for tonight FOMC: the Fed holds rates unchanged, likely 10-2, Warsh keeping a hawkish more work to do message because inflation is sticky near 3% rather than accelerating, so UBS expects 25bp hikes in December and January. Markets price about 10% odds of an October hike versus 92% for December. UK Autumn Budget is expected cautious because fiscal headroom has fallen from 23.6bn pounds in March toward 10bn pounds, so the Chancellor rebuilds only a roughly 15bn pound buffer via smaller tax rises while deferring welfare cuts to 2027. UBS models a bank levy rise from 3% to 6%, cutting NatWest and Lloyds EPS 3-4% and Barclays and HSBC 1-2%. Equinor 3Q26 operating earnings beat 1% at 12.4bn dollars, adjusted operating profit beat 4%, but net income missed 15%, while FY production guidance was raised to 4% from 3%.
